serviceCards.title: Game & High Fence Installation
serviceCards.desc: Eight foot high fence for whitetail, exotics and hog control, built with fixed knot wire and braced corners that stay tight for decades. We handle clearing, layout and water gaps so the whole perimeter holds.

serviceCards.title: Pipe Fence & Corrals
serviceCards.desc: Welded pipe fencing, corrals and working pens built from new or used oilfield pipe, set in concrete and welded on site. It's the toughest fence you can put around horses and cattle.

serviceCards.title: Barbed Wire Fencing
serviceCards.desc: Four, five and six strand barbed wire with class 3 galvanized wire and proper H-brace corners. Most pastures run $2 to $4 per foot installed, and we'll walk the line with you before we quote it.

serviceCards.title: Ranch Entrance Gates
serviceCards.desc: Pipe entrance gates, overhead arches and cattle guards that swing true and make the front of your place look right. We build them to fit your drive, from a simple 16 foot gate to a full custom entry.

aboutBlurb:
Brazos Ridge Fence Co. builds working fence for working land. From an 8 foot game fence around a whitetail place to five strands of barbed wire across a cow-calf pasture, we build it the way old fence hands did, with deep-set corner posts, real H-braces and wire stretched until it hums. We also weld pipe fence and corrals and hang ranch entrance gates that still swing straight ten years on.

We give you real numbers up front, not a sales pitch. Barbed wire usually runs $2 to $4 per foot, net wire $3 to $5, game fence $4 to $8 and pipe fence $12 to $25, and our ranch fence cost guide breaks all of it down by the foot and by the mile. If a storm drops a tree on your fence or cattle get out on the highway, our emergency line answers 24/7 at (509) 351-8404.

faq.q: How much does a game fence cost in Waco?
faq.a: Most 8 foot game fence in Central Texas runs $4 to $8 per foot installed, which works out to roughly $21,000 to $42,000 per mile. Heavy brush clearing, rocky ground and extra gates push the number up, so we quote it after walking your line.

faq.q: Do you charge extra for after-hours emergency calls?
faq.a: Yes, after-hours and weekend emergency calls carry a $150 to $250 trip fee on top of the repair, depending on how far out you are. If cattle are out on a road we treat it as a priority call and we'll usually have wire back up the same night.

faq.q: How tall does a game fence need to be for deer?
faq.a: Whitetail need a fence at least 8 feet tall to be reliably contained, and Texas high fence rules apply if you're managing deer behind wire. We build game fence at 8 feet with fixed knot wire, which also does a good job slowing feral hogs.

faq.q: How long does it take to fence 10 acres?
faq.a: A 10 acre perimeter is roughly 2,600 feet of fence. With normal clearing, a crew typically finishes barbed wire in 3 to 5 working days, while game fence or pipe fence takes longer because of the heavier posts and wire.

faq.q: Do you clear brush along the fence line?
faq.a: Yes, we clear cedar, mesquite and brush along the fence line as part of most jobs, and we price it separately so you can see the cost. A clean line makes for a straighter fence and a lot less maintenance down the road.

We work out of Waco and cover McLennan, Bosque and Falls counties, including China Spring, Crawford, McGregor, Valley Mills, Lorena and West. Estimates are free and in writing anywhere in that service area.
